trigger.method: trigger-runner.mjs: the description is copied verbatim into a probe skill in a fresh project, and each query runs as a nested `claude -p` with no user settings, plugins, hooks or MCP. A run counts as TRIGGERED only when the Skill tool fires for that probe. best_score and accuracy are over (case, rep) rows.

acceptance.method: diagnostic (generate with-guide vs isolated baseline, LLM judge vs rubric acceptance)
acceptance.verdict: Guide-following output hits all 8 rubric acceptance points (probe-first path decision, Contract+delete-When-to-Activate, looping Before-you-finish, rubric.json with escape hatch, conv1-read-back/conv2-reask, sidecar+plugin.json+README, mandatory meta:skill-eval); isolated baseline misses nearly every one — it even explicitly keeps '## When to Activate' (contradicting the standard), invents a differently-named/located acceptance file, and skips the probe, the conversation-reopening rule, the sidecar/version bump, and any measurement step.

checklist.note: the edited block is a shell snippet and prose addressed to the author
the named scripts write only under .claude/hillclimb/ and the skill's evals/result.json
no embedded key, token or credential
the snippet runs repo scripts whose only deletes are their own temp sandboxes and that sandbox's auto-memory dir; no destructive command in the skill
no external host beyond the nested claude -p the skill already documented
no sudo, setuid, cron, shell profile or launch agent
